lesson_topic: Climate Change — Weather vs. Climate: Fundamental Differences

principles.evidence: No non-decorative graphics, diagrams, charts, or data figures are present across any of the five slides; all slides are text-only. The visual channel carries no imagery to pair with the narration, violating the core multimedia condition.

On-screen text consists of full, multi-sentence paragraphs verbatim matching the transcript narration on every slide. The transcript does not elaborate beyond or diverge from the on-screen text in any substantive way.

All complex descriptions are rendered as dense on-screen prose rather than being reserved for narration, placing the entire informational load on the visual-text channel. The narration is written as natural spoken language in places, but it mirrors the on-screen text verbatim, eliminating any modality split.

No decorative imagery or extraneous anecdotes are present; all content is topically relevant to the weather-vs-climate distinction. Slide 5 contains garbled on-screen text ('the hottest in over years'), indicating a rendering artifact that introduces noise, partially undermining this criterion.

Slide titles provide a minimal visual hierarchy, and the narration uses some verbal orienting language (e.g., 'to contextualize this,' 'conversely'), but no arrows, highlights, color contrast, callouts, or emphasis cues are present on any slide. No single takeaway is visually emphasized or centered on any slide.

Because no graphics are present, criteria requiring label-to-graphic proximity, integrated captions, or visual connections between terms and referents cannot be met. Text content is grouped under slide titles without any spatial separation of distinct concepts, partially satisfying the layout-coherence criterion.
